# comment to appear in the port. A row here excuses ONE oracle comment line, and only because
# the row proves, mechanically, one of two things (`_g3b_not_carried.py` holds every rule):
#   no-counterpart  the comment sits on reference code the port does not have by a RECORDED
#                   gate checks that `decl` is DECLARED in the oracle file (not a keyword or a
#                   common local), that the comment is attached to it, that no Rust item or
#                   field anywhere in the workspace has any G1 name form of it and no `///`
#                   doc or `PORTS:` comment cites it (a renamed counterpart), and that the
#                   evidence record (<= 30 lines) names `decl` AND the oracle file and carries
#                   no strike or RESOLVED/PORTED marker anywhere.
#                   RATIFICATION for code comments). The evidence record must list this
#                   `file:line`. The text may carry no digit, identifier, backtick, ALL-CAPS
#                   token, technical term, or word of the surrounding oracle code, unless the
#                   reason is `MIXED-CARRIED: "<port comment>"` and that comment is in the port.
# WHAT THE GATE CANNOT DO: judge whether a recorded decision is RIGHT. Evidence written by
# the same batch that adds the rows satisfies the checks trivially, so every new or edited
# evidence record, and every new row, needs a human reviewer. Where the reference code has
# a Rust site at all, the port's convention is to QUOTE the comment there with a PORT NOTE,
# Every row must match the oracle line AT THE PIN (`ORACLE_PIN`) verbatim and still be MISSING
# or REVIEW in the port: a row the port now carries is STALE and RED. Excused comments are
# printed as `NOT-CARRIED (<class>)`, never hidden. Idiom collapses with no recorded decision
# (an arena, an infallible arm, an argv) are NOT rows: those comments are carried, quoted with
# a PORT NOTE, at the Rust site that replaced the code.
# Columns (tab-separated): oracle_file (relative to the oracle's src/), line, class, decl
# (`-` for gag-prose), evidence (`<doc>#<literal needle>`), text (the comment, marker
